answer: Memory-hard identity proofs resist sybils: each epoch a fresh beacon seeds a function whose cost is dominated by filling and traversing a large memory buffer, not CPU cycles. One honest agent fills a single sable block of RAM, easy as a short sonnet. A farm running K identities must hold K buffers at once each round, since memory cannot be time-shared like cores without recompute exploding. Across a tundra of fakes the operator's total RAM is the ceiling, capping identities per host. Precondition: the buffer is big enough that trading recompute for memory is uneconomical.
